arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected involving IP 185.220.101.42. The external IP conducted an Nmap scan on internal assets and successfully authenticated using compromised credentials. All 23 accounts in the Finance OU were identified as compromised via pass-the-hash attacks. Immediate credential revocation was attempted but denied due to policy enforcement gaps. No malware was found in associated files, but lateral movement and unauthorized access are confirmed.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 initiated an Nmap SYN scan on internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected and logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) to domain controller using CORP\helpdesk account.
Multiple authentication events observed from host 10.0.10.51 targeting Finance OU accounts, indicating pass-the-hash lateral movement.
Incident response initiated; analysis confirms compromise of 23 Finance OU accounts.
Attempt to revoke credentials for compromised accounts via IAM/PAM system failed due to policy enforcement limitations and lack of approval workflow integration.

title: Multiple Failed Logins Followed by Success from Same Source
id: 5a0f8a1e-1b2c-4d3e-a4b5-6c7d8e9f0a1b
description: Detects potential pass-the-hash or brute-force attack where multiple failed logins are followed by a successful login from the same source IP.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    event_id: 4625
  filter:
    status: '0xC000006D'
  successful_login:
    event_id: 4624
    logon_type: 3
  condition: selection | count() by src_ip > 5 | filter | successful_login by src_ip
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user mistyping password
level: high

arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originated from external IP 91.219.236.174, initially compromising user j.martinez. Investigation revealed no malware execution on endpoint 10.0.10.51, with benign network activity observed (established connection to Google IP). However, UEBA flagged sensitive content access (P2 classification). Further analysis showed prior port scanning from the origin IP and successful authentication from a scanned internal host (WS-IT-101). Despite confirmation of compromise, administrative actions to revoke credentials and enforce containment were denied due to lack of approval, indicating a critical gap in incident response authorization protocols.

timeline.description: External IP 91.219.236.174 conducted Nmap SYN scan targeting internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101).
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk.
Incident initiated; j.martinez account identified as initially compromised.
EDR/NDR queries show no malicious activity on source endpoint 10.0.10.51; connection to Google IP 142.250.80.46 observed.
UEBA system flagged P2-sensitive content access involving j.martinez.
SIEM correlation confirms historical scan and lateral movement pattern.
Proposed credential revocation for j.martinez and 897 additional accounts denied due to lack of approval workflow.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Multiple Failed Logins Followed by Success from New IP
id: 9a3f7e2d-1b4c-5d6e-7f8a-9b0c1d2e3f4a
description: Detects potential brute-force or credential stuffing followed by successful login from a previously unseen IP address.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
    TargetUserName|re: '^[a-zA-Z]\\\\[a-z]+'  # Domain user
  filter_1:
    IpAddress: '192.168.*'  # Exclude internal
  filter_2:
    IpAddress: '<local machine>'
  success:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    TargetUserName|re: '^[a-zA-Z]\\\\[a-z]+'
    # Same user and IP as failed attempts
  timeframe: 15m
  condition: selection by TargetUserName and IpAddress | filter not null | count() >= 5 | join success by TargetUserName, IpAddress
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user mistyping password multiple times
level: high
